function: Excluded (above_phy): learned UAV-to-cluster trajectory assignment and per-step SN selection (TDMA association); transmit power fixed, no learned physical-layer decision (pp. 5, 9, 11).
notes: Reason 4 (above_phy). Both learned agents act above the physical layer. The high-level Pointer-TP agent assigns each UAV to an SN cluster, i.e. UAV trajectory planning (p. 9: the output is the index of the cluster assigned to each UAV; p. 1: it 'assigns each UAV to an appropriate cluster'). The low-level RA agent picks the SN that each UAV serves at each TDMA time step, i.e. user association or scheduling (p. 11: 'The RA agent determines the association between the UAV and the SNs in the assigned cluster at each time step'; p. 4: TDMA protocol). The transmit power is a constant (p. 5: 'the transmission power is a constant'), and no beam, bandwidth or power is learned (Table I, p. 12). Borderline point for the reviewer: the paper names the second agent 'resource allocation', and the aerial-link clause treats learned resource allocation as physical layer, but here the only 'resource' allocated is the choice of SN per time step, which is scheduling. If the reviewer reads it as physical-layer resource allocation, the work would be area 6 (single-antenna Rician A2G links, p. 4; quantitative simulation results, Figs. 8-16).
